correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: The <a> tag creates anchor elements (hyperlinks). Remember: 'a' for 'anchor' - it anchors one document to another.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: The <a> tag creates anchor elements (hyperlinks). Remember: 'a' for 'anchor' - it anchors one document to another.

questions.question: The href attribute contains the link's ______.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: href contains the link's destination - where it goes when clicked. It can be a URL, file path, email address, or page section.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: href contains the link's destination - where it goes when clicked. It can be a URL, file path, email address, or page section.

questions.question: To open a link in a new tab, add target="______".

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: target="_blank" opens links in a new blank tab/window. The underscore before 'blank' is required.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: target="_blank" opens links in a new blank tab/window. The underscore before 'blank' is required.

questions.question: Email Us creates an email link.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: mailto: is the protocol for email links, just like https: is for websites. It tells the browser to open the email client.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: mailto: is the protocol for email links, just like https: is for websites. It tells the browser to open the email client.

questions.question: For same-page navigation, use href="#______" with an element's id.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: Use href="#idname" to jump to an element with id="idname". The # symbol indicates you're linking to an ID on the same page.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: Use href="#idname" to jump to an element with id="idname". The # symbol indicates you're linking to an ID on the same page.

questions.question: Good link text should ______ where the link goes.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: Link text should describe the destination. Screen reader users often navigate by links, so descriptive text is essential for accessibility.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: Link text should describe the destination. Screen reader users often navigate by links, so descriptive text is essential for accessibility.

questions.question: Links typically appear ______ and underlined by default.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: Most browsers display unvisited links as blue and underlined. This visual cue helps users identify clickable elements.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: Most browsers display unvisited links as blue and underlined. This visual cue helps users identify clickable elements.

questions.question: A link without an href attribute is a ______ link.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: Links without href are placeholder links - useful during development but should be replaced with real URLs before launching.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: Links without href are placeholder links - useful during development but should be replaced with real URLs before launching.

questions.question: About links to a file in the ______ folder.

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: Using just the filename (about.html) means the file is in the same folder as the current HTML file.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: Using just the filename (about.html) means the file is in the same folder as the current HTML file.
